claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-09-27, ccusage 20.0.26 (tag v20.0.26, commit d9821088b98aa536c7a385aa1a4579d6fa02269b, released 2026-09-27T16:26:00Z) was qualified and switched in, reopening qualification as the 2026-09-26 publication trigger requires. The npm tarball https://registry.npmjs.org/ccusage/-/ccusage-20.0.26.tgz (24,216 bytes) had sha256 b8d59c191f357d5e847c109f306cf522e60496fc9219be2ab72d201fd59eb1f2, and its sha512 and sha1 matched the registry integrity and shasum. At that commit the upstream Rust suite (cargo test --workspace, Rust 1.97.1, in an environment mirroring nix/tests.nix) exited 0 with 944 passed, 0 failed and 3 ignored, and the Node tests passed 34 of 34. On the native_token_ci synthetic fixture the installed 20.0.24 and 20.0.26 executables returned byte-identical output: 2 rows, 1,900 input, 380 output and 2,430 total tokens, and a totalCost within 1e-9 of 0.0328. On the host's native histories, daily, weekly and monthly token totals were identical between the two versions; 20.0.24 left claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6-luna unpriced there, and 20.0.26 left no model unpriced. A synthetic pricing probe gave claude-opus-5-5 a cost of 0.0 on 20.0.24 and 4.0 on 20.0.26 for 1,000,000 input tokens, with a claude-opus-5 control at 5.0 on both. The coordinator repointed the production launcher to 20.0.26 at 2026-09-27T22:01:01Z; the read-back resolves it to the 20.0.26 prefix, which prints 'ccusage 20.0.26', and the 20.0.24 prefix is retained for rollback.
limitations: macOS is registry-only: the macOS pin carries the same tarball digests, but no Mac installed or ran 20.0.26, and @ccusage/ccusage-darwin-arm64@20.0.26 stays unpinned (its registry integrity is recorded in data only).

The pinned sha256 covers only the npm launcher tarball (5 files). The Rust executable comes from the optional dependency @ccusage/ccusage-linux-x64@20.0.26, which npm resolves at install time outside that hash; this receipt records its registry integrity but did not compare it with the installed copy.
npm dist.gitHead is null, so the tarball binds to commit d9821088 only through the git tag. The registry lists an SLSA provenance attestation for 20.0.26, which was not fetched or verified here.

Upstream CI was not reproduced: nix flake check, nix build .#ccusage-tests, just test-node under pnpm 12.5.1, the Nushell contribution-gate test and the Babashka compare-pr-performance test did not run (Nix, just and pnpm are absent). The Rust suite ran under an isolated rustup 1.97.1 toolchain with a script mirroring the nix/tests.nix environment, not inside the Nix derivation, and the Node tests ran on Node 24.21.0.
The Node tests do not discriminate this bump: the two test files are identical between v20.0.24 and v20.0.26.

The native-history comparison covers one range (2026-09-20 to 2026-09-26, with rows only for 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-26, Claude and Codex together). It shows token parity between the versions, not agreement with provider billing, and session and blocks reports were not compared.

20.0.26's cost figures use upstream snapshot prices. On the same tokens the range's totalCost rose from 3423.92 (two models unpriced) to 9894.33; neither is a qualified contract price, and the recorded use commands keep --no-cost.

The landscape winner pin in catalogs/landscape/foundation.json stays 20.0.24 (manifest-20260922), so a 20.0.26 host receipt needs scripts/host_receipts.py record --allow-unbound-version and stays unbound until a new verdict wave. No host receipt is recorded here.
The launcher repoint is the coordinator's operation; this receipt records its time and a later read-back, not the operation's own output.

The daily native-history comparison is a coordinator record from 2026-09-27T21:50Z whose argument vector was not retained (data.native_checks.native_histories.daily.retained_output); only its JSON outputs are. The weekly and monthly comparisons and the pricing probe record their commands.
New hosts receive this pin only after the next release tag.
